title: Prompt-cache TTL per agent role
brief: Parked: workers on 5m cache TTL, waiting sessions on 1h — operator deciding
body:
Claude Code gives a subscription's main session a 1-hour prompt-cache TTL (cache write 2× base input) and subagents/forks 5 minutes (1.25×); every lyx agent is a main session in tmux, so all of them write at the 1-hour price (see https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching.md).

Measured on the `landing` run's transcripts: Discussion, Plan, Bouncer and Burler never paused more than 90 s between turns, so 5 minutes keeps them warm; ly-drive paused up to 508 s (three gaps over 5 minutes), so it needs 1 hour. Webster Master waits on forks via Monitor and is not yet measured.

Likely shape: shuttle sets `CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=5m|1h` (Claude Code v2.1.242+) per role when it spawns a session, configurable per role. loomyard was developed with the 5-minute limit in mind, so 5 minutes matches its design assumption.

title: Burler: round-N focus directive conflicts with the read-prior-rounds-last rule
brief: Focus directive needs prior-round files the round prompt says to read only after the review
body:
Friction from run `operator-surface`, Burler Webster-Review round 2 (stencils from `d619100af`).
The round-2 focus directive asked the reviewer to check the round-1 F4 site list and the round-1 fix commits, which requires reading `round-1-review.md` and `round-1-fixer-report.md`.
The round prompt's instruction 2 says prior-round files are read only after the review is saved, so the focus file handed over in instruction 1 cannot be followed without breaking it; the reviewer read them early and said so.
Fix direction: the focus directive restates the sites it depends on, or the prior-round rule exempts what a focus directive names.

title: ide hub workspace: review follow-ups
brief: Small cleanups from the PR #301 review
body:
Follow-ups from the PR #301 review (`85902381e`), all non-blocking:
- `internal/fabricengine/hubworkspace.go` builds the prime path by hand (`filepath.Join(l.HubPath, primeName, l.AnchorRel)`) instead of `WorktreePath`.
- `internal/ideengine/spawn.go` now WARNs on every spawn whose prime resolution fails, task spawns included (silent before).
- Removing the last pair prunes `_portals/<anchor>`, so the hub workspace shows a missing folder until the next prime spawn.
- Relative-path settings spliced from the prime into the workspace file resolve against `_launchers/`, not the prime.

title: loom start races the ly-drive self-removal and ends with no driver
brief: First loom start after a hand-back keeps a strand that is about to be removed
body:
After a hand-back, the ly-drive session removes its own strand with a detached `lyx reed remove --name loom-driver --detach` that waits for the session's pid to exit (end-of-session command from `083e992cf`).
A `lyx loom start` issued in that window sees the loom-driver strand still live, keeps it instead of spawning a driver, and the detached remover then deletes it: the run is left with no driver and nothing happens (hit on `batten-hub-ready` and `focus-marker-warn`, 2026-09-30; a second `loom start` works).
Fix direction: `loom start` treats a driver strand with a pending self-removal (or whose claude has exited) as gone and spawns a fresh one, or the remover skips a strand that was re-adopted since it was scheduled.

title: Integration tests leave tmux sockets behind
brief: reed/loom tests leak tmux servers and sockets in /tmp
body: Tests leak tmux sockets: `/tmp/tmux-1000/` holds hundreds of `lyx-Test…`, `lyx-contract-…` and `lyx-warp-bare-…` sockets left by reed/loom integration tests. Test fixtures should kill their tmux server and remove the socket in `t.Cleanup`.

title: Landing verify gate skips a merge interrupted before its marker write
brief: A crash between the merge-in commit and the pending-verify marker write leaves the next resume seeing up-to-date with no marker, so verify is skipped.
body:
Found reviewing PR #308 (`publish-verify-after-merge`).
Fabric reports a finished-but-interrupted merge as already up to date, so the gate cannot tell a verified tree from an unverified one.
Robust fix: record the task HEAD that last passed verify, and verify whenever HEAD differs from it.

title: Worktree-Create should wait for the prime lock instead of blocking
brief: Parallel `lyx batten run` starts: every run but the first blocks at Worktree-Create on the held prime run.lock and needs a manual resume.
body:
Starting three `lyx batten run` at once blocked two at Worktree-Create: "prime lock .../.lyx/shed/run.lock is already held; another batten producer is creating or tearing down a task worktree".
The lock is held only for the seconds a create or teardown takes, so the producer should wait for it (bounded, e.g. a few minutes) rather than halt; the hub starts runs in parallel as a matter of course.

title: fabric remove leaves the pair tmux session alive
brief: After `lyx fabric remove` the pair tmux session (driver claude, status strand, bash) keeps running in the deleted directory; its late writes recreate the worktree dir as a stray folder.
body:
Seen 2026-09-30 for quarry-cli-answers and status-strand-by-driver: after landing and `fabric remove --remote`, their reed sessions were still alive hours later.
A driver that wrote its stop report after the removal recreated `<hub>/<slug>/.lyx/...` and `<hub>/<slug>/_lyx/shed/<slug>/drive-reports/<report>.md`: a stray directory, and a drive report that never reached the archive.
The hub killed the sessions and deleted the dirs by hand.

Fix: remove (and batten teardown) ends the pair reed session (reed down) before deleting the worktrees, and waits for or refuses on a live driver; a stop report written after done should land before the archive tag.
